subject: MSA + Order Form: proposed limited carve-out for trade-secret-triggered damages
messages:
From: Markus Berg <markus.berg@novamed.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Stevenson <elena.stevenson@novamed.com>
Date: Mon, May 3, 2027 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: MSA redlines — carve-out for trade-secret losses

Priyom,

Thanks for walking through the MSA last week. Our legal team pushed back on Section 9 (Limitation of Liability) and suggested a narrow carve-out: in the event of a confidentiality breach that results in unauthorized acquisition or disclosure of Novamed trade secrets, Novamed will require damages outside the general liability cap.

We attached our redlines (Novamed_MSARedlines_v3.docx) — the key language they want is a sentence that removes the liability cap for "willful or grossly negligent misappropriation of trade secrets resulting in demonstrable economic harm."

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood legal confirm whether you can accept an exception scoped to "willful misappropriation of trade secrets" (not ordinary negligence)?
- If not, what is the alternative you can accept (e.g., higher dollar cap, or a multiplier tied to fees)?

We need to present a clean position internally on Wednesday afternoon — is it possible to get a proposed counter-redline by EOD Tuesday?

Thanks,

Markus
Markus Berg
Head of Legal — Novamed Health
markus.berg@novamed.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, May 3, 2027 at 11:08 AM PDT
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — carve-out for trade-secret losses

Markus — thanks for the note and the redlines. We're aligned that trade-secret misappropriation is a meaningful risk and worth special handling.

Looping in Karthik (legal) and Monica (CS/Compliance) to draft a targeted alternative that preserves Redwood's overall liability framework while addressing Novamed's concern. High-level we can move on two paths:

1) Narrow exception: remove cap for proven willful misappropriation of trade secrets leading to demonstrable economic loss, with strict proof requirements (forensic report, admission, injunction).
2) Compromise cap: maintain cap for ordinary claims but raise/uncap for trade-secret claims when willfulness is shown — or set a defined elevated cap (e.g., greater of actual damages or 12 months of fees, subject to evidence).

We will aim to get a clean counter-redline for you by EOD Tuesday. Monica — please confirm the operational evidence we can reasonably provide if Novamed requests forensic logs/evidence. Karthik — please propose draft language and any conditional controls (e.g., indemnity, notice windows).

Best,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
pri yom.das@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Markus Berg <markus.berg@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, May 4, 2027 at 08:43 AM PDT
Subject: RE: MSA redlines — carve-out for trade-secret losses

Priyom / Markus — I reviewed Novamed's proposed sentence and drafted a targeted alternative intended to be a middle ground. Key elements:

- Scope: carve-out limited to "willful and knowing misappropriation of trade secrets" as defined by applicable law (not simple negligence).
- Trigger: Redwood's obligation to pay damages outside the cap only arises upon (a) a judicial determination, or (b) a settlement accompanied by an independent forensic report establishing misappropriation by Redwood personnel or contractors.
- Remedy cap: if judicially determined as willful misappropriation, Redwood proposes damages equal to actual proven damages without a pre-set cap; for settlement scenarios we propose an elevated cap equal to the greater of (i) 12 months of Redwood's fees paid by Novamed under the Order Form, or (ii) documented direct economic loss, capped at USD 3,000,000 — this is to avoid open-ended exposure while being commercially meaningful.
- Controls: prompt notice (30 days) and cooperative forensic process; Redwood retains right to participate in any forensic investigation and to seek injunctive relief first.

Draft redline (proposed insertion to Section 9):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, in the event of willful and knowing misappropriation of Novamed's trade secrets by Redwood or its agents, and upon a judicial finding or a settlement supported by an independent forensic report, Redwood's liability for such willful misappropriation shall include proven direct damages. For settlement scenarios, liability shall be limited to the greater of (a) twelve (12) months of fees paid under the Order Form, or (b) documented direct damages, in no event to exceed Three Million United States Dollars (USD 3,000,000), unless a court awards a greater amount following a finding of willful misappropriation."

Rationale: the judicial/forensic trigger narrows exposure to cases with substantive evidence; the elevated cap for settlement balances Novamed's need for recovery with Redwood's responsibility to maintain insurability and predictable risk.

Monica — operationally we can provide audit logs, access records, and assistance from our security team; however, we will ask for confidentiality and limited use terms in any forensic report. Markus — please let us know whether Novamed's legal can live with the judicial/forensic trigger and the proposed settlement cap mechanics.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Markus Berg <markus.berg@novamed.com>

Cc: Elena Stevenson <elena.stevenson@novamed.com>
Date: Wed, May 5, 2027 at 02:55 PM PDT
Subject: Re: MSA redlines — carve-out for trade-secret losses

Karthik / Priyom — thanks for the thoughtful proposal and for narrowing the scope. Novamed's internal counsel reviewed and has two main points:

1) Judicial finding: we understand Redwood's preference for a judicial finding as a hard trigger, but Novamed can't commit to waiting for court outcomes in every case. We would accept a settlement trigger only if the settlement amount is supported by an independent forensic report prepared by a neutral third-party acceptable to both parties.

2) Cap size: the proposed USD 3,000,000 cap is a good starting point for mid-market customers, but Novamed is asking for a firm carve-out to at least USD 10,000,000 for trade-secret misappropriation caused by gross negligence or willful conduct. Alternatively, Novamed will accept an uncapped judicial remedy but wants the settlement cap set at 10 months of fees or USD 10,000,000, whichever is greater.

Would Redwood leadership consider escalation for strategic deals (we're at commit and expect meaningful volume in year one)? If you can mark the proposed redline as "leadership confirm" and indicate whether an escalation to accept an elevated cap for strategic accounts is possible, we can keep the commercial close moving.

Also: please confirm the exact forensic artifacts Novamed would need and the timeline Redwood would be able to produce them — internal procurement will want those details before approving.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Regards,
Markus
